They often display this "domineering posture" in front of the camera, which is interpreted by fans as a symbol of confidence and dominance.

It was originally planned to be released in January 2026, but was postponed to May at Blumengarten's request. The song's central refrain "Du bist gut genug" (German: "You are good enough") is sung in falsetto by Blumengarten member Rayan Djima.

It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Strong protectiveness: Highly sensitive to the safety and interests of the partner, tending to take the initiative to clear obstacles and solve difficulties for the partner, often manifesting a "you don't have to worry about it, I'll handle it" attitude. Preaching tendency: I like to give life suggestions and advice as a person who has experienced it, with an elder-like reasoning tone in my voice, such as "You can't do this" and "Listen to me. You are right." The classification culture of XX boyfriend/girlfriend has experienced an evolution process from subdivision to generalization on the Chinese Internet: Embryonic period (about 2018-2019): Japanese classification concepts such as "dog type" and "cat type" entered the Chinese online community. In the early days, they were mostly seen in character discussions in the ACG (anime and game) circle, and have not yet spread to love topics on a large scale.
memes.culture_en: Daddy-type Boyfriend is a popular term used on the Chinese Internet to describe a specific type of boyfriend. It is part of the "XX-type boyfriend/girlfriend" character classification culture. This classification system is deeply influenced by the concept of "kei" (けい) in Japanese subculture - in Japanese animation and idol culture, characters are often divided into "dog type", "cat type", "salt type" and other types based on personality characteristics. After this classification method was introduced to China, it was fermented by social media and gradually evolved into a localized love personality labeling system.
memes.use_en: Scenario type Usage example Social platform discussion Xiaohongshu note title: "Are dad boyfriends really good? Let me talk about my daily life compared with my dad's boyfriends" Emotional content Bilibili/Tik Tok video title: "Dad boyfriends vs puppy boyfriends, which one do you choose?" Fan circle evaluation Fan comments: "His role in the new drama is really a daddy, so secure!" Love live sharing Moments/Weibo: "Today I was urged to drink hot water by my dad's boyfriend again. Really a modern old father." Memes/emoticons with text: "Daily life of dad's boyfriend: drink more hot water.jpg" "Put on long johns when the weather is cold.jpg" Pros and cons debate Douban post: "Why am I becoming more and more disgusted with dad's boyfriend?

memes.name: 哈兰德吃人
memes.literal_en: The core meaning of "Harland eating people" is an exaggerated metaphor for Harland's court dominance and brutal scoring ability. New star-fan interaction model: Haaland's initiative to engage in posts and enter Chinese social platforms has broken the traditional image of aloof players and created a lively and down-to-earth "Internet celebrity" personality, providing a new paradigm for Internet marketing of sports stars. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Visual symbol: Harland’s celebration after scoring a goal with his teeth bared and a ferocious expression was pictured as a funny scene of “eating people” or “selecting meals”. Extended meaning: Majin Buu: Because of Haaland's strong performance and celebrations on the field, Chinese fans compared him to the devouring villain "Majin Buu" in "Dragon Ball", which became his classic Chinese nickname. Overseas budding stage (2020–2021): Haaland’s highlight performance and ferocious celebration expressions during his time in Dortmund spawned "child-eating" jokes on European social media.
memes.culture_en: "Haaland eats people" (also often called "Haaland eats children") is one of the most famous Internet memes in the global football circle in recent years. Its protagonist is Norwegian football superstar Erling Haaland. This meme does not refer to violence in the literal sense, but is an extremely exaggerated humorous metaphor for Haaland's terrifying scoring efficiency, ferocious playing style and unique personal image on the court. The origin of this meme can be traced back to Haaland's time at Dortmund (2020–2022).
memes.use_en: Scenario type Usage examples Meme packs and memes. Netizens posted pictures of Haaland and children together as a "meal selection" with the text "dinner is served" and "how many to eat tonight". Stadium commentary. After Haaland scored, the commentator joked that "Majin Buu eats people again" and "scored another one. How many bowls of rice will I eat today?" Opponent fans ridiculed. Wolves and other rival fans joked after Haaland scored that "the ogres scored again and ate people", using memes to dispel the aura of the superstar. Brand Advertising and Marketing Nike released a pseudo-documentary to interpret the plot of "eating children"; brands such as Wanglaoji and Qingyang used memes in their advertisements Social media interaction Haaland himself responded to Chinese netizens' "eating light rail" meme in Chinese and filmed a funny video of swallowing Chongqing's Liziba light rail Canteen/cooking scene Netizens paired the image of Haaland's goal with the text "It's time to eat, it's time to eat", combining it with the "food man" culture

memes.literal_en: Basic definition: The "Jiangpanya" meme is derived from the classic reversal lines in the AI short drama "Snow Mountain Rescue Fox". The core dialogue template is: A: "Have you ever rescued a fox in the snow mountain? Commercialization sample of AI short drama: Ailin Junji's team verified the commercial feasibility of the AI short drama with extremely low production costs, triggering the industry's attention to the AI content production model. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: " A: "I'm not a fox, I'm the salted duck! "——I'm not here to repay a favor, I'm here to take revenge. AI short drama boom period (mid-March 2026): The short video series "Snow Mountain Rescue Fox" was released on Douyin and other platforms. The first episode received tens of millions of views at a very low cost, quickly attracting attention.
memes.culture_en: In March 2026, Ailin Junji, a Guizhou new media team composed of four people, used AI tools to produce a Shaw Brothers martial arts-style short drama "Snow Mountain Rescue Fox". The first episode cost only about 40 yuan to produce, but unexpectedly received more than 5 billion views, detonating the entire network. The core idea of this AI short drama subverts the traditional classic narrative of "the fox fairy repays a favor". The plot is roughly as follows: A knight rescues a white fox in the snowy mountains.

memes.name: 走个面儿
memes.literal_en: "Going for a face" is a colloquial expression in Beijing, and its core meaning revolves around the culture of "face". Reflection on integrity in the entertainment industry: The incident triggered widespread public discussion on celebrities using their influence to ask fans to "pay the bill." Many industry insiders called on the industry to respect the audience's right to make independent choices. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: For example, "I'm going to have a quick meal before leaving this dinner party." Give a face, give a face: Ask the other party to cooperate or participate in something out of kindness. The incident outbreak stage (June 17-19, 2026): Han Hong's "face-to-face" speech at the premiere of "Catch a Spy" was filmed by the audience and uploaded to the Internet, quickly becoming a hot search on Weibo. A large number of media and self-media followed up with reports, and the topic’s reading volume exceeded hundreds of millions in a short period of time.
memes.culture_en: "Zhao Ge Mian'er" is a colloquial expression with Beijing dialect color. The literal translation means "to show up, to go through the motions", and the extended meaning is "to give face, to reward face". It is often used to request the other party to come to support or to show favor. This phrase belongs to the Jianghu circle language in Beijing's Hutong culture, and is not an orthodox daily spoken language in old Beijing. Outbreak On June 17, 2026, the film "Catch the Spy" directed by director Feng Xiaogang held its premiere in Beijing.
memes.use_en: Scene type Usage example Original event Han Hong shouted at the premiere, "We brothers and sisters in Beijing, come out and help bring the first round of box office." Internet meme. Netizens left a message in the comment area, "The boss asked me to work overtime on the weekend, so I went out" for self-mockery. Social ridicule. Posted in a friend group chat, "Come out and help me get a knife from Pinduoduo." Ironic usage The comments section satirizes celebrities, "People's face is worth money, and we have to pay for it out of our own pockets." Self-deprecating life, "I went to a meeting today just to show up, and I came back without saying anything." Cultural Interpretation, Self-media article analysis, "Why do you need to pay for a visit? The answer is hidden in five thousand years of Chinese characters."

memes.name: 等待一生的巨浪
memes.title_en: Waiting for the big wave of a lifetime
memes.literal_en: Basic definition "Waiting for a huge wave of a lifetime" literally means "spending a whole life waiting for a huge wave". The core conveys the emotional state of "waiting for a major change"**. Emotional outlet: In a fast-paced social environment, "Waiting for a Lifetime Big Wave" provides young people with a literary channel to express their anxiety and expectations, and alleviates uncertainty about the future through poetic language. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Feeling of powerlessness about the current situation: In a more negative context, it expresses the regret and self-deprecation of "waiting all my life but getting nothing", which is a metaphor for the disappearance of life in the ordinary. Self-motivation: In a positive context, it means "ready to go, waiting for the big wave that belongs to me to come" - believing that life requires patient accumulation and waiting for the wave of the times that belongs to you. "Waiting for a lifetime" does not originate from a specific film or television work or celebrity quote, but a collective expression that naturally grows out of content creation on social media. Emotional copywriting period (approximately 2020-2021):;
memes.culture_en: "Waiting for a lifetime of huge waves" is an emotional expression phrase widely spread on online social platforms. Its core image comes from the metaphorical connection between "waves" and "waiting for life". The phrase is composed of two images: "waiting for life" and "big waves". "Waiting for a lifetime" emphasizes the long span of time, with a sense of fate and persistence;
memes.use_en: Scenario type Examples of use Short video copywriting A video on Douyin with a picture of a huge wave hitting the shore, with the copy saying "Waiting for a huge wave of a lifetime, even just once" Emotional complaints Expressing career/relationship difficulties on Weibo or Moments: "Living the same days day after day, as if waiting for a huge wave of a lifetime" Self-mockery Self-mockery under workplace/academic pressure: "I have been waiting for the big wave all my life, but before the wave comes, I am already lying flat" Inspirational quotes Xiaohongshu notes are accompanied by pictures of sunrise/ocean: "Don't worry, the huge wave you have been waiting for your whole life is on its way."

memes.name: 妙脆角小猫
memes.literal_en: Basic definition Literal meaning: Describes cute pets such as kittens and puppies with two pointed ears or two tufts of hair on their heads. The shape resembles the conical shape of the snack "Miao Crisp Corner". New paradigm of cute pet content: This meme provides a low-threshold, high-distribution dubbing template for cute pet short videos. Bloggers only need to take pictures of the "pointed corners" on the top of their pets' heads and add audio to participate, which greatly stimulates the enthusiasm for UGC creation. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Extended meaning: Cute identity label: When a person or image is said to have "two horns on its head", it means that it has the attribute of being cute and is a member of the "Cute Horn Family", conveying a contrasting cuteness of "Although I have horns, they are harmless". Pretend to be stupid and respond in a stunned manner: derived from the classic reply sentence pattern - "I don't understand what you are saying at all, because I have two crispy corners on my head". It is used to express "I don't understand what you are talking about" or deliberately act cute to avoid the question, similar to the cute version of "In one ear, it goes in and one ear goes out." The birth of the dubbing template (late May 2026): The cute pet dubbing video released by the blogger "Bao Chef" became popular on Douyin. The audio of "Two Crispy Corners on the Head" was quickly imitated by a large number of people because of its magical rhythm and cute pictures. The early videos were mainly about real cats and dogs, and the hashtag #This is me with crispy horns on my head quickly accumulated views.
memes.culture_en: The "Miao Crispy Corner Kitten" meme originated from a cute pet dubbing template video posted by Douyin blogger ** "Bao Chef". In the picture, a kitten with two tufts of fur or two ears standing on top of its head is accompanied by a naive narration: "This is me. There are two cute corners on my head. Then it can be turned into a bunny or a puppy. And then its nose is a sliced shiitake mushroom, which is also very cute."** Because the two symmetrical sharp corners on the cat's head resemble the familiar puffed snack "Bugles" in everyone's childhood, both in shape and expression, this metaphor quickly became fixed and became a universal text template.
memes.use_en: Scene type Usage examples Cute pet video Add the audio of "two crispy horns on the head" to a kitten with two tufts of hair on its head to show the cute moment of the cat. Game creation The operator with long ears in "Arknights" and the horn-like decorated character in "Fearless Contract" were dubbed by fans with this audio. Social reply When faced with a topic that you don't understand or don't want to respond to, reply "I don't understand what you said, because I have two crispy horns on my head" Celebrity/anime clip Match the cute looks of celebrities such as Song Zuer and Ma Jiaqi with the audio to highlight the cuteness of the characters. Emoticon packs/avatars Use the image of "Crispy Kitten" to express the emotions of "I have nothing to do with you" and "I don't understand".

memes.name: 你是龙子你是虾子
memes.title_en: You are a dragon, you are a shrimp
memes.literal_en: You are a dragon, you are a shrimp is a typical homophonic meme. Its cleverness lies in the complete overlap of the pronunciation of Chinese characters: Basic definition: dragon (lóng zǐ) → is pronounced exactly the same as deaf (deaf person). You are a dragon and you are a shrimp reflects a trend of "anti-swearing" expression in contemporary Internet culture - young people no longer use straightforward swear words to reply, but use homophonic memes and irony to complete social criticism while maintaining a sense of humor. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: On the surface it means "You are the son of the dragon, you are the son of the shrimp", but actually it alludes to "You are deaf, you are blind" - that is, a person "pretends to be deaf and dumb" and turns a blind eye to certain things. Extended meaning: Discourage swearing behavior: The core context of the meme is "Swearing is wrong behavior". When someone uses uncivilized language on the Internet, use this sentence to remind the other party euphemistically and humorously - "Are you deaf and can't hear how unpleasant your words are, or are you blind and can't see that everyone is disgusted? You are a dragon, you are a shrimp. Meme on June 7, 2026 The prototype began to appear on the Douyin platform around the same time. During the same period, there were also variations such as "Are you a dragon or a shrimp" (#志民 # Willow Zhimin #karina related) and "You are a dragon crocodile, you are a shrimp" (#五人性 related). As of June 19, 2026, "You are a dragon, you are a shrimp!"
memes.culture_en: "You are the dragon, you are the shrimp" is an Internet buzzword that quickly became popular on the Douyin/TikTok platform in June 2026. This meme first appeared in a short video on Douyin. The video is only 2 seconds long. The picture is accompanied by the text "You are a dragon, you are a shrimp!", conveying the core message in a minimalist form.
memes.use_en: Scenario types Examples of use: Douyin comment area Reply "You are a dragon, you are a shrimp" when encountering trolls or online scolding, euphemistically pointing out that it is wrong for the other person to curse. Social media mutual hostility. Use it on Weibo, Tieba and other platforms to replace direct insults to form an "advanced insult" effect. Friend teasing. Use it when joking among friends, implying that the other party is "pretending to be deaf". Internet etiquette education. Use it as a humorous way to remind others to pay attention to civilized online language.

memes.name: 青蛙教练
memes.literal_en: Coach Frog refers to the frog doll used by Team Spirit to replace the real coach during the IEM Cologne Major 2026, and the series of online cultural contents derived from it. Major event cultural symbol: Coach Frog has become an iconic memory point of the IEM Cologne Major 2026, alongside the classic off-field scenes in previous Majors (such as the "olofmeister jump sniper" at the 2018 Boston Major, etc.). It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Identity positioning: Since Spirit's two coaches hally and S0tF1k were unable to attend, donk arranged for them to "sit" in the coaching bench in a playful way, becoming the team's mascot and "tactical guide". The extended meaning of "no need for a coach" ridicule: After Spirit "led the team" with a frog coach to achieve a winning streak, netizens joked that "a truly good team does not need a coach" and "this frog knows tactics better than Hally." Emergency phase (June 4-6, 2026): Spirit head coach hally was hospitalized, assistant coach S0tF1k’s visa was denied, and the team faced the dilemma of having no coach before the start of the IEM Cologne Major.
memes.culture_en: Coach Frog is a hilarious internet meme born during the 2026 IEM Cologne Major "Counter-Strike 2" (CS2) event. This meme originated from the classic scene in which the CIS giant Team Spirit (Green Dragon) was unable to attend due to visa issues for the coaching team. The talented young player Donk placed a frog doll behind the players to act as a "temporary coach". On June 4, 2026, Spirit officially announced that head coach Hally was unable to travel with the team due to hospitalization;
memes.use_en: Scenario type Usage example Live event barrage When the director cuts to the camera of Coach Frog, the barrage floods the screen with "Quack Gua Gua", "Professional Coach", "Coach Says Rush B" Community second-generation video Bilibili, Douyin has a large number of UP main productions "Frog Coach Interview", "Frog Coach Tactical Layout" and other dubbed funny videos Social media jokes Weibo, Hupu, Tieba netizens commented on the Green Dragon game and ridiculed "Quickly watch the interview with the Green Dragon coach!" Live broadcast goods/merchandise meme: "Donk the same style Frog Coach" doll product appeared on Taobao and Xianyu, and the price was ridiculed as "increasing from 17 yuan to 39 yuan 6". Match commentary interaction. The commentator mentioned "Frog Coach's tactics worked" when Spirit paused or won a key point.

memes.name: i昴TV
memes.literal_en: iPleiades TV can be broken down into three parts i + Pleiades + TV: Basic definition i: It is not only the English letter "i", but also a homophone of the Chinese "爱" (ài), forming a pun. A new paradigm of barrage culture: "iPleiar TV" combines character names with TV channel formats to create a new way of interacting with barrage. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: TV: Imitates the naming format of a TV channel, implying that this is an "exclusive channel with Subaru as the protagonist." Therefore, "i Subaru TV" contains two meanings at the same time: "i Subaru TV" - "a channel that loves Subaru", expressing fans' love for the character. Infancy (Re0 seasons 1 to 3): Natsuki Subaru frequently experienced tragic deaths due to his "death return" ability in the early plots. Fans have begun to tease the protagonist's "suffering constitution" in various ways. The term "iPleiades" took shape during this period, but it has not yet formed a fixed "iPleiades TV" format.
memes.culture_en: iSubaruTV is a popular barrage meme in the fan circle of the anime "Re: Life in Another World from Zero" (referred to as Re0 / Re:Zero). It is mainly active on Chinese social platforms such as bilibili and Douyin. The core of this gag lies in the clever disassembly and reorganization of the name of the protagonist Subaru Natsuki (なつき すばる). "Subaru" is the core character in Natsuki Subaru's name, and "i Subaru TV" imitates the naming format of TV channels (such as HBO, MTV, etc.), packaging it into an exclusive channel with "Subaru" as the protagonist.
memes.use_en: Scene type Example of use Animated barrage Re0 When Natsuki Subaru was pushed down the stairs and fell to his death in the fourth season, the barrages collectively read "i Subaru TV, you win" Video title Station B Re0 Second creation video title uses "i Subaru TV" and "爱subaru TV" as tags, such as "Status eight episodes ago: sunny and cheerful big boy; status after eight episodes: i Subaru TV you win" Douyin short comments Douyin Re0 "i Subaru TV, Natsuki Subaru is loved again" appears in the comment area of the edited video to express sympathy and ridicule for the character's experience. When discussing the Re0 plot in social discussion forums and post bars, "i Subaru TV chapter" is used to describe a particularly sadistic plot arc. Derived variants such as "Still Love Subaru TV", "Favorite Subaru TV", "Ai Subaru TV Another Masterpiece", are used in different suffering scenes.

memes.name: 躲春
memes.literal_en: The core meaning of hiding from spring is to avoid conflicts or negative relationships with the outside world by being alone, sitting quietly, etc. during a specific period of time during the Beginning of Spring Festival. The return of cultural identity: The popularity of hiding in spring reflects contemporary people's renewed attention to traditional solar terms culture as a link between the laws of nature and personal life. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Specific groups of people: Mainly those who are guilty of Tai Sui (those who conflict with, punish, harm, or break the zodiac of the year) and those whose age is nine (the imaginary age includes 9 or multiples of 9). For example, 2026 is the year of the Bingwu Horse, and people born in the year of Horse, Ox, Rat, and Rabbit are considered to need to hide from spring. Folklore continuation stage: It has long existed in the cognition of rural areas and the older generation. As a numerology taboo passed down from word of mouth, it lacks extensive social discussion. Internet Renaissance Stage (2020 to present): With the rise of “New Chinese Lifestyle” on platforms such as Xiaohongshu and Douyin, Zangchun has been rediscovered by Generation Z because of its strong sense of ritual.
memes.culture_en: Hiding Spring, also known as "Hiding Tai Sui" or "Hiding Spring", is a special custom related to the Beginning of Spring solar term in traditional Chinese folk culture. Its theory is rooted in the understanding of "magnetic field conversion" by ancient astrologers and folk beliefs. The ancients believed that the beginning of spring is the moment when the old and new years change. At this time, the magnetic field is extremely chaotic and powerful. If a person's zodiac sign conflicts with the "Tai Sui" of that year (i.e., commits a Tai Sui violation), he or she will be susceptible to aura collision, causing fluctuations in fortune throughout the year.
memes.use_en: Scene type Specific usage and meaning Folk custom practice Around 4:02 am on February 4, 2026 (the beginning of spring), the person who committed Tai Sui sat quietly in the room alone. Social media: Post "I'm hiding from you today, I won't reply to messages" in your circle of friends as a personal display of your social status. Workplace ridicule: When faced with a heavy workload, he joked: "I am hiding from spring. Don't come to me for troublesome things, for fear of disturbing your aura." Health and wellness Combine hiding from spring with "solar terms and health care", meditate, close your eyes and relax, don't stay up late, and don't watch TV dramas.

memes.name: 立春立蛋
memes.title_en: Egg-raising at the beginning of spring
memes.literal_en: Egg-standing at the beginning of spring (also known as "erecting eggs at the beginning of spring") refers to a traditional custom and interesting challenge of trying to erect eggs on a flat surface on the day of "beginning of spring", the first of the twenty-four solar terms. Cultural inheritance: Let intangible cultural heritage such as the twenty-four solar terms be accepted by Generation Z in a more interactive way. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Folk custom sustenance: It means the arrival of spring and the recovery of all things, and symbolizes that in the new year, "people stand firm", "step by step" and "good luck comes with spring". Extended meaning: Ritual social networking: In modern social networks, this has evolved into a "punch-in" solar term celebration, which is a manifestation of contemporary young people's pursuit of "a sense of ritual in life". Traditional custom stage (ancient times - 2000s): Mainly existing as a regional folk custom, it is an interesting part of the series of activities such as "Bite the Spring" and "Dash the Spring" at the beginning of spring.
memes.culture_en: Standing eggs at the beginning of spring originated in China and is said to have a history of more than 4,000 years. Historical background: This tradition was first popular in the Jiangnan area of ​​China. The ancients believed that "Li" represents the beginning, and the beginning of spring is the first of the twenty-four solar terms, marking the change of the year and the intersection of yin and yang. Around 2010, the Meme Encyclopedia: Meme List recorded the clues of the spread of "the beginning of spring and the establishment of eggs". Existing materials can confirm that it enters the public eye mainly through Internet expressions that can be quoted repeatedly, and is written in a fixed way in forwarding, imitation, and secondary creation; however, the data is not enough to prove that a single account is the absolute first release, so the archives describe the source as a "currently verifiable communication node" and do not fictionalize the sole inventor.
memes.use_en: Scene type Specific performance and meaning Social media Post the "#立春立蛋challenge" on Douyin, Xiaohongshu and other platforms, with photos of success to pray for good luck throughout the year. Family interaction: Parents take their children to play the egg-standing game as a traditional cultural enlightenment that is both educational and entertaining. Campus Education Physics teacher explains scientific knowledge such as friction, center of gravity and balance through egg-standing activities. Fishing in the workplace: Putting eggs on the desk on the day of the beginning of spring means "the foundation of the workplace is solid" and is a metaphysical way to reduce stress in the workplace.

memes.name: 芭比Q了
memes.literal_en: The homophonic pronunciation of the English word "barbecue" was said by game anchors as "Barbie is Qing", and then expanded from "being barbecued" to a light disaster broadcast of "it's over, completely hopeless". From an archival perspective, what really needs to be recorded is how it was understood and reused, not just repeating the name in a different way.
memes.meaning_en: There is no longer a requirement to be popular after spreading. Any plans that are ruined, exams are overturned, equipment is damaged, or deadlines are forgotten, you can say "Now Barbie Q". memes.name: 社交恐惧症（社恐）
memes.literal_en: 1. Basic definition Medical original meaning: A mental disorder manifested by pathological fear of social situations, which may be accompanied by physiological reactions such as rapid heartbeat, sweating, and trembling. Changes in the social paradigm: This has given rise to the popularity of services such as "zero-contact delivery", "self-service checkout", and "online reservations". These business models have alleviated the survival pressure of social phobes to a certain extent. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: It refers to those groups who feel tired in social interactions, avoid unnecessary social interactions, or act reserved in front of strangers, which does not necessarily reach a pathological level. 2. Related derivative words: pseudo-social phobia: refers to a person who is submissive in front of strangers, but is "socially awesome" in front of acquaintances. Medical terminology stage (before 2010): “Social phobia” mainly appears in medical popular science articles, with low public awareness and a certain negative bias. Subculture identity stage (2016-2020): Influenced by Japan’s “otaku culture” and Nordic “border culture”, young people began to gain legitimacy for “not participating in low-quality social interaction” by admitting their “social fear”.
memes.culture_en: Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD), referred to as "social phobia", was originally a rigorous psychological and medical term, which refers to an individual's significant and persistent fear, anxiety, and avoidance behavior in social situations. In the Chinese Internet environment, the memeization of the word "social fear" began around 2016. With the rise of social platforms such as Weibo and Douban, young people began to use this word to describe their embarrassment, withdrawal or discomfort when facing unfamiliar social scenes. In 2018, images of "Finnish social distancing" (such as queuing two meters apart at a station) went viral on social media, giving rise to the concept of "spiritual Finns" and further promoting the popularity of "sociophobia" as a subcultural label.
memes.use_en: Scenario type Typical performance: Encounter in the elevator: When you see a neighbor or colleague walking towards the elevator, in order not to say hello, you will pretend to play with your phone or wait for the next one. Answering the phone: Seeing an unknown caller will cause anxiety (telephone phobia), and one would rather communicate through typing on WeChat. For workplace social networking, "transparent people" in team building activities should try to sit in the corner to avoid becoming the center of the topic or being named by the leader. Party Scene: During a dinner party, the person lowers his head the whole time while eating, or relieves embarrassment by repeatedly going to the bathroom or looking at his mobile phone.

memes.name: CP
memes.literal_en: Basic definition: Character pairing: refers to the setting of two characters (usually fictional characters) as lovers or intimate relationships in literary and artistic works. It is common in fan creations and fan discussions. Cultural creation: CP culture has spawned a large number of fan works. There are more than 2 million CP-oriented works in the Chinese area of AO3 platform alone. It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Extended meaning Fanquan culture: CP has become an important part of the fan economy, giving birth to a special group of "CP fans" who specifically support the pairing of a certain pair of stars or characters. Commercial marketing: Movies, TV dramas, and variety shows often attract audiences and increase topicality by “speculating on CP.” Fan culture stage (2005-2015): CP is mainly limited to the two-dimensional fan circle, focusing on the pairing of animation and game characters, and the main communication channels are post bars and forums.
memes.culture_en: CP is the abbreviation of Couple in English. It originally originated from Japanese fan culture and refers to the creative act of pairing two characters into a couple or having an intimate relationship in literary and artistic works (especially animation, film and television, novels, etc.). This concept can be traced back to Japanese doujinshi culture in the 1970s, and was introduced to China through the Internet in the 2000s, becoming an important part of ACG (animation, comics, games) culture. In the Chinese Internet, the popularity of CP began in Baidu Tieba and Jinjiang Literature City around 2005. At that time, a large number of fan creators began to use "CP" to refer to their favorite character pairings.
memes.use_en: Scenario type Usage examples Fan creation Create fan novels or comics of "Shield Iron" (Captain America × Iron Man) CP on Lofter, AO3 and other platforms Fan circle discussion Weibo super chat "Lang Lang Ding" gathers CP fans of "The Order of Mountains and Rivers" starring Zhang Zhehan and Gong Jun The CP setting of "Land Couple" (Lu Han × Dilmurat Dilraba) in the variety show "Run" triggers heated discussions across the Internet Daily ridicule Posted in Moments "Today my bestie and I wore couple's outfits, we are the best besties CP of the year"

memes.culture_en: Bagpipes are heard from afar. They were originally the lyrics of the song "Obviously" from Jay Chou's 2012 album "12 New Works". The original sentence is "Bagpipes are heard from afar, and I only care about the news about you." It depicts the romantic mood of longing. The internet meme was born in January 2023. In the comment section of a video exposing a barbecue vendor taking money from an elderly person, the Douyin user @訳风声风pipis (later known as "Gun Ge" by netizens) replied "Go away" to netizens who defended the vendors, and later replied "Go away too" to those who tried to stop the fight, forming a straightforward style of "indiscriminate insults". The contrast between the ID and the behavior quickly aroused attention, and the number of followers increased by hundreds of thousands in a few days.

memes.name: 思密达
memes.literal_en: Original semantics and grammatical function: an honorific suffix with no actual meaning in Korean, similar to the "le" and "ah" at the end of a Chinese sentence. Language penetration: Promoting "Korean drama style" to become a specific expression paradigm on the Chinese Internet (such as verb postposition). It expands dissemination through imitable scenes and secondary creations.
memes.meaning_en: Internet Semantics Joking and Imitation: Adding "Smecta" at the end of a Chinese sentence creates a "pseudo-Korean Chinese" humorous effect (for example: "Today we eat barbecue Smecta"). Ironic expression: When used in a yin and yang context, it may imply sarcasm (for example: "You are so smart Smecta"). Stage evolution Cultural input period (2005-2012); the popularity of Korean dramas drives language imitation, and variety show subtitle groups such as "I Am a Singer" strengthen the stereotyped perception of "Smecta = Korean".
memes.culture_en: Seumnida is derived from the Korean honorific suffix "습니다" (pronounced: seumnida). It is the standard honorific suffix for Korean declarative sentences and is used in formal occasions to express respect for elders, superiors or strangers. This usage can be traced back to the court etiquette of the Joseon Dynasty, and was later spread to the Chinese Internet through modern Korean dramas, news broadcasts and other media. After 2010, as Korean dramas such as "Dae Jang Geum" and "My Love from the Star" became popular in China, "Smecta", as the most recognizable Korean element, was widely imitated by Chinese netizens, gradually deviating from its original meaning and evolving into a "joking language symbol."
memes.use_en: Usage scenarios Typical examples Social media memes Use "laughing to death Smecta" in the Weibo/TikTok comment area to enhance humor Video content creation The UP host of Bilibili imitated Han Zong's tone and said "Follow Smecta three times in a row" Cross-cultural communication Chinese netizens use "안녕하세요Smecta" to poke fun at Korean greetings Product marketing E-commerce platforms use "Authentic Kimchi Smecta" as a promotional rhetoric
